description: Elixir accepts `Kernel.<>("--", r)` in a pattern and matches it like `"--" <> r` (checked with elixir 1.19.4: prints {:long, "hi"}). fz refuses it with parse/concat-pattern-operand (fixture 00674), because pattern decoding runs before alias resolution and only trusts the expander-stamped call (`__fz_from_operator__`) or the bare operator. Done when: a spelled-out Kernel.<> / List.concat in a pattern, resolved through aliases, decodes to the same pattern as the operator on interp, run and build; 00674 becomes an oracle fixture; a user alias that shadows Kernel is not fooled.
title: [BUG] A spelled-out Kernel.<> or List.concat call in a pattern means the operator, as in Elixir
